hypotheses.note: LocallyConnectedSpace X (T2Space X, IsRigidAction G X only for the gx bridge and the gx-style corollary); the analyticity of the family of models (gx's IsAnalyticModelFamily) is not used

DEC-25: [SingularGXStructure G X M], the ported maximal a.e. (G,X)-atlas; the X_A-part weakened: only the singular points of M need an X_A-chart (hcov), where gx's X_A-atlas covers M and its charts have connected image and a centre sent into S_alpha; gx-style form existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25_of_isAEMorphism takes gx's (U, V, phi : U =~ V, IsAEMorphism phi) at each singular point

every chart of the maximal a.e. atlas (into X) and every IsAEChart into a model space (an a.e. isomorphism of an open subset of M onto an open subset of a model, = gx's notion by isAEChart_iff_isAEMorphism); question 2

hypotheses.paper: (a) X causally arc-connected, G acts by morphisms (l.619)
(b) the causality of X_alpha extends the natural causality of reg(X_alpha) (l.620)
hypotheses.note: hreg: every chart of the maximal a.e. atlas of X_alpha is an isomorphism onto X; implied by (b) (the natural causality of reg(X_alpha) makes every chart of its maximal atlas an isomorphism, and these are the charts of the maximal a.e. atlas, IsMaximalAEAtlas.mem_of_compatible), equivalent to it given hb and OQ-18's uniqueness; the reading of the graduated Causal.GXSingular, now over gx's atlases

(b'), hiso: every a.e. isomorphism between open subsets of the model spaces (IsAEChart G X psi, psi : X_a -> X_b, DEC-62's local form) is an isomorphism of topological spacetimes (ChartIso (DY a) (DY b) psi). It is exactly what the conclusion needs: forall_exists_causality_singularGX_iff (under (a), (b), existence for every such M iff (b')); at regular sources it holds anyway (chartIso_model_of_subset_reg)
unique among absolutely minimal causalities (OQ-18, open); one isomorphic chart at each point suffices for uniqueness

findings: ETT.tex:631-632: hypothesis (B) is justified by 'transition maps are restrictions of elements of G and of isomorphisms of the model spaces', which treats the isomorphisms of the model spaces as isomorphisms of topological spacetimes; neither (a) nor (b) (l.619-620) says so, (b) fixing the causality of X_alpha on reg(X_alpha) only. Under DEC-25 the transition between two X_A-charts at a singular point is an a.e. isomorphism between open subsets of models (IsAEChart.trans, IsAEChart.symm). Lean: under (a) and (b), the proposition's existence half holds for every singular (G,X)-manifold whose singular points lie in X_A-charts iff every such isomorphism is an isomorphism of topological spacetimes (forall_exists_causality_singularGX_iff; take M = X_alpha with its identity chart). Suggested addition to (b): 'and every isomorphism between open subsets of the model spaces is an isomorphism of topological spacetimes'. No Lean counterexample to the printed form: lean-causal has no singular (G,X)-structure with a singular point (gx's BTZ models are not ported). Informally (not formalized): one singular model carrying two causal arc-connected causalities which agree on its regular part and differ at a singular point gives two models satisfying (b) with the identity an a.e. isomorphism between them and no causality making both identity charts isomorphisms; an analytic family (gx's def:family_singular_manifolds_endowed) forbids that between distinct models at points of S_alpha, but constrains neither the automorphisms of one model nor the points of sing(X_alpha) outside S_alpha.

ETT.tex:628-632 (carried over from Causal.GXSingular, now over gx's atlases): the second half of (b) is what (B) needs across a chart into X and an X_A-chart (ChartIso.agreeOn_of_isAEChart: at a regular point the X_A-chart reads, in charts of the maximal atlases, as an element of G), and the proof cites (b) for (A) only.
Uniqueness: as for prop:GX_espace_temps_topo, false in the library's gluing-free reading of defi:causalite, proved among absolutely minimal causalities (OQ-18).

(C) Baire is not needed (OQ-10); the analyticity of (G,X) is used only as local connectedness of X (and T2 + rigidity for the bridge to gx's subtype notion); the analyticity of the family of models is not used.

Non-vacuity: singularGX_dec25_line instantiates every hypothesis (a), (b), (b'), the covering of the singular locus, on M = R with one model R (translations, timelike line) and proves the causality produced is the timelike line; its singular locus is empty, so (b') is exercised only at regular points.
questions: Is (b') -- every isomorphism between open subsets of the model spaces is an isomorphism of topological spacetimes -- part of what 'analytic singular structure (G,X,X_A)' or 'model space' means (the thesis), or should (b) state it? Reading taken: an added hypothesis, in DEC-62's local form; the row stays partial. Lean shows it is necessary and sufficient given (a), (b).

Which charts are 'the charts (U,Y,V,phi) of A' of a (G,X,X_A)-manifold? Reading taken: the maximal atlas, as DEC-16 for (G,X)-manifolds: every chart of the maximal a.e. atlas and every a.e. isomorphism of an open subset of M onto an open subset of a model; gx's X_A-charts (connected image, centred at a point sent into S_alpha) are among them, so the conclusion covers them, and the hypothesis asks charts only at singular points. Over a given X_A-atlas only, the conclusion is weaker.
Uniqueness rests on OQ-18 (open): proved among absolutely minimal causalities.

labels.label: rem:hypotheses_proposition_prop_gx

hypotheses.note: as the proposition's conclusion for M and N: causalities C, C' making every chart of the maximal a.e. atlases and every X_A-chart an isomorphism, C absolutely minimal, the singular points of N in X_A-charts (existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 produces them under (a), (b), (b')); (b') itself is not used again

f a local homeomorphism (unbranched), singular points allowed: strongMorphism_of_isAEMorphism_of_isLocalHomeomorph; without singular points (Sing M = empty, f(M) in Reg N) with (a) alone: strongMorphism_of_isAEMorphism; at branch points open
strong morphism (DEC-10/DEC-12) where proved; the reduction weakMorphism_iff_of_isAEMorphism is for weak morphisms (no openness is known at branch points)

findings: ETT.tex:635-637: the remark gives no proof. Under DEC-25 it holds for every a.e. (G,X)-morphism which is a local homeomorphism, singular points included: near x, f is an a.e. isomorphism chart e, and e followed by a chart of N at f(x) (of the maximal atlas if f(x) is regular, an X_A-chart if not) is a chart of M at x, so the proposition's causalities make f a local isomorphism (strongMorphism_of_isAEMorphism_of_isLocalHomeomorph). At a branch point f is not a local homeomorphism, does not read in charts as an isomorphism of model spaces, and nothing in (a), (b) or (b') constrains it; weakMorphism_iff_of_isAEMorphism reduces the remark exactly to the points outside Reg(f) = Reg(M) cap f^-1(Reg(N)) (lem:regf1). The printed remark, branch points included, is neither proved nor refuted; it would follow from a condition on the models like (b') for branched maps (every a.e. morphism between open subsets of model spaces is a morphism of topological spacetimes), which the paper does not state.
questions: Is the morphism of topological spacetimes of the remark strong or weak (OQ-19's last question, which DEC-25 does not answer explicitly)? Reading taken: strong where proved (unbranched maps), weak in the reduction to the points outside Reg(f).

Is a hypothesis on the branched morphisms between model spaces (the analogue of (b') for non-invertible maps) intended for the branch points? Reading taken: none; the row is partial, proved for unbranched maps.

(G,X)-atlases are in lean-causal (T-ett-gxsingular-dec25): CausalScaffold.Port.Portly and .Port.SingularAtlas, verbatim (GX.x as Causal.x); a singular (G,X)-manifold is [SingularGXStructure G X M] (maximal a.e. atlas, DEC-25), Reg/Sing/aeAtlas/IsRegularOn/IsAEMorphism/regLocus as in gx. An X_A-chart without subtypes is Causal.IsAEChart G X e (CausalScaffold.GXSingularDEC25), equivalent to gx's a.e. isomorphism of open subsets (isAEChart_iff_isAEMorphism); open subsets carry gx's induced structure (instance opensSingularGXStructure, restated from gx's SingularII/Tame).

Checking a gx -> Causal port by elaborated types without building lean-gx: run the toolchain's lean on a probe with LEAN_PATH = lean-gx/.lake/packages/*/.lake/build/lib/lean : lean-gx/.lake/build/lib/lean (read-only, no lake in lean-gx); in both environments rename GX.x -> Causal.x in .const AND .proj nodes (projections carry the structure name) and compare Expr.hash of every constant's type and value, kind, universe parameters, reducibility, instance status (T-ett-gxsingular-dec25: 281 + 8 constants identical).

In a port, `omit [inst] in` changes the elaborated type when gx kept the unused instance argument (gx files with `set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false`): use `set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in` instead, or the type hashes differ.

Causal.IsComplete (the port of gx's a.e.-atlas notion, CausalScaffold.Port.SingularAtlas) shadows mathlib's root IsComplete inside namespace Causal for every importer (kb/0016): write _root_.IsComplete for uniform completeness there.
A local `have key : ∀ {Z : Type*} ...` cannot be used at two universes (the level is a metavariable, not generalised): state such a step as a top-level lemma.

prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo under DEC-25 needs (b'): the isomorphisms between open subsets of the model spaces are isomorphisms of topological spacetimes; it is necessary and sufficient given (a), (b) (Causal.forall_exists_causality_singularGX_iff).
